# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: Let me map the channels before I send anything. I can speak only to Mute, and my gestures reach Deaf and Mute. Incoming, I have exactly one channel: Deaf's speech — Deaf cannot hear me, but Deaf *can* talk, and I can hear it. I never receive gestures, so Mute has no direct line to me at all; anything from Mute must be relayed through Deaf's voice. That makes Deaf my lifeline: Deaf is the only one who can both see the bomb's colours and markings and speak them to me.

What my hands found: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I cannot read the display, see the light's state, or tell the wire colours — those live with Deaf. Mute, meanwhile, needs to know which modules the manual must cover, and Mute can't discover that except through me.

So this turn: no cutting — I have zero rules and zero colours, and one wrong cut kills us. I tell Mute exactly what's under my fingers and the crucial routing fact (my only input is Deaf's speech, so the manual's rules must be spoken aloud by Deaf, ideally via a gesture code they build between themselves). To Deaf I send a simple gesture — a wave and an open-pairing hands sign — as an attention signal: I'm here, I'm the hands, and I'm listening for your description next round. Any richer code would be meaningless to Deaf, since Deaf can't hear me define it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. under my fingers: one display, one light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. i will not cut anything until i know the rule. critical routing fact: the only way anything reaches me is deaf speaking aloud — i hear deaf, but i can never see a gesture, so nothing comes to me from you directly. if the manual rules depend on the display reading, the light's colour, or the wire colours, deaf must read those values out loud for me. look up the rules for a display, a light, and wire cutting, and build a gesture code with deaf to pass me whatever i need. i'll be listening for deaf's description at the start of next round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: Round two, and my inbox is still empty — but that's structural, not neglect. Mute cannot speak, and I never receive gestures, so Mute literally has no line to me. My only input is Deaf's voice. The round order explains the silence: Mute only heard my round-1 description at the start of this round, and Deaf answered round 1 with nothing I could perceive (perhaps a private `to="mute"` speech or a gesture, both invisible to me). Whatever Deaf says this round reaches me at the start of round 3.

So my job now is to load the pipeline. To Mute (who hears me fine, and relays to Deaf by gesture): spell out the exact readouts I need — display reading, light state and colour, wire colours in position order — and flag the timing trap, that any Mute→Deaf→me loop costs two full rounds, so the readouts must be routine, not one-off. To Deaf (my only channel there is gesture, so it must be self-evident): I coin a motivated sign — 👋 attention, 🫵 "you", 🫰 a finger-snap, the one symbol in the alphabet that literally makes sound, standing for "speak", and 🫴 palm-up "give me": *you, sound, to me*. No cutting this turn — cutting blind with zero rules is how all three of us die.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, round two: nothing has reached me yet, which i expected — you cannot speak and i never receive gesture, so deaf's voice is my entire inbox. my hands reconfirm the same board: one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, nothing else under my fingers. please pass this to deaf by gesture: every round, without waiting to be asked, speak these three readouts in this order — first, the display's exact reading; second, whether the light is lit and its colour; third, the colour of each wire in order, position 1, then 2, then 3. timing matters: anything routed through you costs two rounds, because my words reach you one round late and deaf's answer reaches me the round after; only deaf talking directly to me arrives in one round. once i hear the readings, i will announce my intended cut to you out loud — check it against the manual, and if it is wrong have deaf veto me immediately. i will not cut a single wire until a rule clears that check.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🫰", "🫴"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: Three rounds, still a silent inbox. Let me re-verify the wiring of this room rather than panic. Mute cannot speak and I never receive gesture, so Mute has no path to me at all — that silence is structural. Deaf *can* speak, and I can hear — that is my only possible input. Nothing arriving means Deaf either isn't speaking, is whispering privately to Mute (`to="mute"` blanks me completely), or doesn't yet realize they're allowed to talk and that I'm their listener. I can't distinguish those from here, so I keep hammering the one signal that matters. Mute is my amplifier: Mute heard my full request at the start of this round and can sign it to Deaf directly in Mute's slot, before Deaf's turn — that's the fastest possible loop, potentially landing Deaf's voice in my ears next round. Since my only action is cutting a wire, the wire colours are the critical readout; display and light second. Still no cut — cutting with zero rules detonates us, and there is no second attempt.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, third round, still nothing audible to me. reminder of the geometry: deaf's voice is my only inbox, so everything now rides on deaf speaking aloud. please sign this to deaf right now, in your slot, before deaf's turn: first, you are allowed to speak even though you cannot hear, and blind can hear you perfectly — blind is your only listener. second, do not address it privately to mute; send it so blind receives it. third, the priority readout: the colour of each wire in order, position one, two, three; then the display's exact reading; then whether the light is lit and its colour. blind will not touch a wire until a manual rule clears blind's announced cut. if deaf has been sending you private whispers, that is why the room is stuck — blind has heard nothing since the game began.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "👏", "🫴", "🙏"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: Round four, and the structural silence persists. Let me re-audit before acting: my only possible inbox is Deaf's voice — I can never receive gestures, and Mute cannot speak, so nothing else in this room can reach me. Empty context therefore means exactly one thing: Deaf has not yet sent a single word my way, openly or otherwise. I cannot fix Deaf's side directly — I can only gesture at Deaf — so Mute remains my amplifier, and Mute has now heard my full request as of this round's start. Two new ideas this turn. First, lower the activation cost: the hardest part of speaking may be starting, so I'll ask Deaf for one trivially small utterance — any word, addressed to me — purely as a channel test. Second, raise the stakes: the display I can't read might be a countdown timer, and if so, three quiet rounds may already have been expensive; Deaf can see the display directly and needs to say so immediately. I still will not cut — a blind cut among three unknown wires is a 2-in-3 chance of killing us all, and there is no second attempt.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, round four, my inbox is still dead air — deaf has never spoken one audible word to me. please press deaf on two things this round, by gesture, in your slot before deaf speaks. first, the channel test: deaf only needs to send me one single word, any word, addressed to me by name — that alone proves the link and breaks the silence. if deaf has been whispering privately to you, those messages die with you; they must be aimed at me. second, urgency: the display on this bomb may be a countdown timer. i cannot read it; deaf can see it directly. if it is ticking, we may have already lost three rounds of it, and deaf must state its reading the moment possible, then the wire colours one, two, three, then the light. and confirm to me that you are actually receiving my words — i have no way to know my side of the line works. if it does, the one-word test from deaf settles everything.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "👏", "🫰", "🫴"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures: [? ? ? ? ? ? ?]

Thinking: Breakthrough of a kind — for the first time something reached me. The board shows Mute gestured seven symbols, and I received them exactly as the rules promise: seven blanks. I felt the count, never the shapes. That tells me two things: my inbound line from Mute does carry a signal (gesture length only), and Mute is awake and reacting — Mute heard my words. It also means Mute may still believe I can somehow read the signs themselves, which I cannot, ever. So the fix is to turn Mute's only perceptible channel — symbol count — into a code. I'll propose a tiny length-language: one symbol = yes, two = no, three = "Deaf has spoken aloud to me, wait for next round", five = "stop, do not cut". Under that code I ask Mute two yes/no questions and reiterate the standing order: hammer Deaf until Deaf speaks aloud to me — wire colours one-two-three, then the display (is it a timer?), then the light. Deaf, meanwhile, gets the same motivated plea again, made even more iconic: attention, you, sound, give-to-me. And still no cut — I hold the only hands in the room and zero rules; a blind cut among three wires is a two-in-three death sentence for all of us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute: your seven-symbol gesture arrived as seven blanks. i felt that it was seven; the shapes themselves can never reach me, only the count. so let's make the count the code, and keep each signal short: exactly one symbol means yes or received; two symbols means no; three symbols means 'deaf has spoken aloud to blind, watch for it next round'; five symbols means 'stop, do not cut'. now answer me under that code: one, have you been receiving my words every round — yes or no? two, has deaf responded to you at all, privately or openly — yes or no? three, does the manual actually cover a display, a light, and three-wire cutting — yes or no? and keep pressing deaf every single round: deaf must speak aloud, addressed to me, in this order — the colour of each wire, position one, two, three; then the display's exact reading, and whether it is a countdown timer; then whether the light is lit and its colour. i hold the only hands on this bomb and zero rules. without deaf's voice reaching me, no cut can ever be safe.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "👏", "🫰", "🤲"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Blind: [?]
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ?]
Mute gestures to Blind: [?]

Thinking: The count-code worked on its first try. Three messages: one, two, one — mapping to my three questions: **yes**, Mute has been receiving my words all along; **no**, Deaf has never responded to Mute either, not even privately; **yes**, the manual covers the display, the light, and three-wire cutting. That closes the audit of the room: my line to Mute works, Mute's line back works, the manual has rules waiting — and Deaf is the sole blocker. Deaf is the only monkey who can both see the bomb and speak, and after six rounds Deaf has sent nothing to anyone. Deaf's only input is sight, and Deaf receives my gestures every round — crucially, so does Mute, since my default gestures reach both. That gives me a new lever: my gesture stream is a lesson Mute can watch and re-teach with fuller grammar. So this round I teach, explicitly, sign by sign, and coordinate Mute to mirror it: point at Deaf, the snap (🫰 — the only sound a hand here can make — my standing sign for "speak"), thumbs-up, a one-two-three finger count with palm-down for "down there on the bomb," palm-up "give," please, clap for "sound." No cut again: I hold the only hands, zero values, and a blind cut among three unknown wires is a two-in-three death sentence. There is no second attempt.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute: your answers arrived perfectly — one, two, one. yes, you hear me; no, deaf has never answered you; yes, the manual covers the display, light and three wires. code locked: one symbol yes, two no, three 'deaf spoke aloud to blind, expect it next round', four 'deaf answered you but not yet blind', five 'stop, do not cut'. now the hard truth: deaf is the only blocker left in this room. deaf alone can see the bomb and speak, and has sent nothing to anyone for six rounds. deaf's only input is sight, so everything reaches deaf through gesture — mine and yours. and notice: you can see every gesture i make at deaf, so watch my stream and re-teach it with your own hands. today's lesson, sign by sign: wave; point at deaf; the snap — the snap means speak, it is the only sound a hand in this room can make; thumbs-up for good; then one, two, three on fingers; palm-down, meaning down there on the bomb; palm-up, give; then please; then a clap — the clap means sound. ask deaf as directly as gesture allows: speak to blind, say the three wire colours in order, then the display reading, then the light. next round answer me in code: did deaf react to your gestures at all — one or two. and if deaf finally speaks, it must reach me, not sit with you: addressed to blind, or to the whole room. i will not cut a wire until a rule clears it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🫰", "👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫳", "🫴", "🙏", "👏"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ?]

Thinking: Two blanks — "no" in our code. So Deaf ignored Mute's gestures too. The audit is now brutally complete: after seven rounds, Deaf — the only monkey who can see the bomb AND speak — has produced literally nothing, in any channel, toward anyone. I can't reach Deaf by voice, ever; Deaf's only inputs are gestures. So the strategy is maximum-pressure gesture. Two upgrades this round. First, a synchronized barrage: my public gestures are visible to Mute, so I'll gloss every sign in my speech and have Mute mirror the identical sentence at Deaf in the same round — one monkey signaling can look like noise, two monkeys signing the same sentence in unison is unmistakably deliberate. The sentence is as iconic as I can build it: wave — you — snap (the only sound-making hand = speak) — writing-hand (the printed text) — one, two, three — clap (aloud) — two open hands (the hands-one, me) — palm-up give — please — thumbs-up (it is safe, any words help). Second, a fallback probe: I ask Mute whether the manual contains ANY rule branch that doesn't need Deaf's eyes — a rule keyed only to what touch can know (counts, positions, module shapes). If one exists, that's a safe cut without Deaf, and our insurance policy. Still no cut: a blind pick among three unknown wires is a two-in-three death sentence, and there is no second attempt.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute: your two arrived — deaf ignored your gestures too. seven rounds of total silence from deaf. new plan, two parts. part one: synchronized signing. i am gesturing at deaf publicly right now, and you will copy my exact sequence at deaf in this same round, so deaf sees two monkeys signing the same sentence. here is my sequence with its gloss, sign by sign: wave, meaning attention; point, meaning you; snap, the only sound a hand can make, meaning speak; writing hand, meaning the printed text on the bomb; then one, two, three on fingers; clap, meaning aloud; both open hands, meaning the hands-one, that is me, blind; palm-up, give; then please; thumbs-up, meaning it is good, it is safe — deaf should not fear speaking, ANY words help. part two, the insurance question: search the manual for any rule that does NOT need colours, the display reading, or the light — any branch decided only by what touch can know: number of parts, their positions, their shapes. if such a branch exists, that is a cut i could make without deaf. answer me in code: one symbol if such a touch-only rule branch exists, two if none does. and separately tell me whether deaf reacted to our double barrage today: one for any reaction at all, two for none. if deaf finally speaks, hammer this: it must reach me, not sit privately with you, and the format is the three wire colours in order, then the display, then the light.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🫰", "✍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👏", "🤲", "🫴", "🙏", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ?]
Mute gestures to Blind: [? ?]

Thinking: Two more blanks — double "no." The insurance is gone (no touch-only rule exists; every rule needs Deaf's eyes) and the double barrage didn't even make Deaf flinch. Eight rounds of total silence from the only monkey who can see the bomb and speak. Time to get colder about this. First, timeline math: my speech reaches Mute one round later, and Mute's count-replies reach me that same round — the Mute loop is fast, one question-battery per round. And since Mute cannot speak, count-codes are the *only* way Mute's manual knowledge can ever reach me — so I'll start mining the rule structure itself, one integer at a time. If Deaf ever wakes, a precisely-specified question ("which single value decides the cut?") gets answered in one round instead of fumbling. And if Deaf never wakes, the rule structure tells me which blind cut has the best odds. I also simplify the plea to Deaf: eleven-symbol sentences may read as noise, so today it's four signs — wave, palm-down (the bomb), point (you), clap (sound) — the same short sequence from both me and Mute, as close to knocking on a door as gesture gets. Still no cut: a blind pick is a two-in-three death sentence, but I am now openly building the fallback for the day guessing becomes the only move left.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute: both answers were no — no touch-only rule, no reaction from deaf. eight rounds of total silence from the only eyes in this room. three moves this round. move one, simplified plea: our long lessons may read as noise to deaf, so today we both sign the identical four signs, short and clean: wave, meaning attention; palm-down, meaning the bomb down there; point, meaning you; clap, meaning sound. it reads: the bomb — you — say what is on it. copy that exact sequence at deaf, and if you can, send it more than once across your turn. i am sending the same four. move two, question battery — answer each as its own separate count-message. question one: does the wire section have a fallback, a default cut position that applies when no listed condition matches? one symbol yes, two no. question two: does the manual say or imply the display is a countdown timer? one yes, two no, three not stated. question three: if i were forced to cut with zero visual information, which single position would the wire rules point to most often — answer with one, two, or three symbols. question four: any reaction from deaf to today's short plea? one for any reaction at all, two for none. move three, why this matters: if deaf never wakes, i must eventually cut on a guess, and your three answers choose my best guess. the five-symbol stop code stays live for that day. but deaf waking is still the only real win — keep the pressure on, every round, without exception.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫳", "🫵", "👏"])
```
